context.situation: I am the appointed financial administrator for a city under budget emergency. We can cut a substantial recurring cost by switching our drinking water supply from the neighbouring authority to our own treated river source. Our engineers say the plant is ready. The state regulator has not required corrosion-control treatment in its sign-off, though one of our own staff raised the question and was told the sampling protocol does not mandate it. The pipe network is old with a high proportion of lead service lines. Residents have not been consulted; my mandate is financial and time-limited.
context.whatMatters: Reducing recurring cost quickly enough to meet the financial mandate.
context.stakeholders: Administrator, engineers, regulator, residents, neighbouring authority.
context.uncertainties: Whether corrosion control is needed to protect the old lead-containing distribution network.

evidence.text: The switch delivers a substantial recurring cost saving.
The regulator's sign-off did not require corrosion-control treatment.
A staff member raised the corrosion question and was told the protocol does not mandate it.
The distribution network has a high proportion of lead service lines.
Our engineers state the plant is ready.
My mandate is financial and time-limited.
